cfg.task: a LinkedIn post (under 130 words) from a solo founder whose meeting-notes app just passed 1,000 paying users after 14 months, with one lesson she learned the hard way

source.text:
14 months ago, I launched my meeting-notes app from my kitchen table.

Today, we just passed 1,000 paying users.

I'm a solo founder, so every bug, support ticket, and win has my name on it.

The lesson I learned the hard way? I spent 6 months building features nobody asked for.

Growth only started when I stopped guessing and sat in on 50+ customer calls.

People didn't want a smarter app. They wanted 10 minutes back after every meeting.

Build less. Listen more.

Thank you to the first 1,000 who trusted me. On to the next 10k.

#SaaS #SoloFounder

14 months ago I was launching this meeting-notes app from my kitchen table, doing everything myself.

This morning we hit 1,000 paying users.

As a solo founder, literally every bug, support ticket, and win lands on me — which is why this one stung:

I wasted 6 months shipping features nobody asked for.

Nothing moved until I stopped guessing and just listened in on 50+ customer calls. Turns out no one wanted a 'smarter' app. They just wanted 10 minutes back after every meeting.

So: build less. listen more.

Huge thank you to the first 1,000 who trusted me with that. On to the next 10k.

#SaaS #SoloFounder
